target: USWDS modal interruption use cases and less-disruptive page alternatives
observed_behavior: The USWDS Modal guidance describes a modal as a deliberate interruption that disables interaction with the surrounding page while a focused task or message is addressed. It lists confirmation of consequential decisions, required acknowledgement before proceeding, and supplementary explanation within a current workflow as use cases. It urges considering a less disruptive component first; multistep or complicated flows are better placed on a dedicated page, field-level errors near affected fields, and page-level status messages as page content or alerts. Modals are framed as a last-resort choice, not the default container for content.
context: W07 B4 K3 bounded first-party USWDS Modal reference; source sections: About the modal component; Guidance — When to use the modal component; When to consider something else. Explanatory DESIGN_SYSTEM / OFFICIAL_REFERENCE only; not cross-source or runtime evidence.
limitations: This is first-party USWDS usage guidance for its design-system modal, not a WCAG requirement, universal product rule or observed usability study.
Acknowledgement, confirmation and supplementary explanation are distinct stated contexts; not every dialog must force a decision.
Inline field feedback and dedicated pages are specifically documented countercontexts rather than grounds to prohibit all modals.
No user outcome, prototype interaction, browser or application behavior was measured.
